approval: Not approved. Preserve this proposal and independently revise/reseal the missing requirements before builders or native runs.

feasibility_scope: The declared component/API and currently authored native/geometry/pixel/visual/update routes are technically feasible and reconstruct under the actual frozen APIs. This true value does not approve semantic coverage: several required clauses lack routes, as listed below. No native build or runtime feasibility result is claimed.

issues.title: The acknowledgement false transition has no obligation or executable route
issues.rationale: BRIEF clause 2 requires a second pre-release selection to clear acknowledgement and emit false exactly once. Every public and private route taps choice only once, at action 2. All approved choice-receipt expectations contain only true. The generic choice-selected and choice-receipt obligations therefore omit this branch; successful matrix reconstruction does not verify it.
issues.required_revision: Independently specify and route the pre-release clear transition, including its selected/label/status/enabled results and a successful native stimulus with the exact false callback interval. Preserve the current seal as a prior revision.

issues.title: Acknowledge-under-hold is never exercised
issues.rationale: The routes acknowledge only initial models with both guards true. Seal and coolant holds appear only after the final identity replacement, where acknowledgement has reset to false and no further activation occurs. Thus the clause that acknowledgement cannot override either hold, and the full primary-enabled predicate, lack a verification route for the acknowledged held condition. H1 does correctly cover both guards false for status precedence, but still with acknowledgement false.
issues.required_revision: Add independently approved same-API states/actions which acknowledge each held condition and assess the resulting hold status and disabled primary. Do not count a disabled primary attempt as successful dispatch.

issues.title: Disclosure requirements are only partly represented
issues.rationale: There is one disclosure activation at action 1 and no close activation in any scenario. There is no event rule bound to that action, so disclosure zero-callback behavior is not checked: later choice and request assertions use their own later intervals. The collapsed-content proposition hides only body paragraphs, omitting headings even though the BRIEF toggles heading/body pairs. Disclosure enabled after request is specified by API.md but has neither an enabled assertion nor a post-request activation.
issues.required_revision: Represent and route native open/close behavior, complete collapsed pair absence, disclosure quietness bound to its actual successful activation interval, and its required enabled behavior after request.

issues.title: All-text wrapping is narrower in the atomic questions than in the BRIEF
issues.rationale: The BRIEF requires all text to wrap without line limits. The only wrapping propositions cover the title and expanded body paragraphs. Section headings, subtitle, status and control text have exact semantic-label checks and horizontal clipping checks, but these do not establish untruncated natural wrapping or reject an ellipsis inside the bounds. This matters in the approved narrow/large profile. A source-backed obligation must cover these required text classes without inventing computed SwiftUI font or line facts.
issues.required_revision: Independently add the missing wrapping scope and feasible atomic visual routes, retaining distinct clipping and overlap propositions.

issues.title: Mandatory layout and scrolling ownership clauses have no corresponding route
issues.rationale: The obligation index and questions do not check full-width component canvas ownership, the minimum 16-native-unit status text inset, absence of fixed-height blank spacer rows, or the prohibition on a component nested scroller. The five pixel atoms prove only their approved solid sample strips. In particular the status sample spans 1.2–3.5% of the semantic band and cannot establish a 16-unit text inset. Full parent sweep coverage proves reachability, not which object owns scrolling or why content is tall. Internal nominal spacing tokens and status minimum height are correctly advisory; this finding does not turn them into measured MUSTs.
issues.required_revision: Give each mandatory structural/layout clause an independently approved feasible evidence route and ownership. If the current collector cannot support a mandatory exact quantity, report that limitation in the revised design review rather than substituting fabricated computed facts.

issues.title: The independently authored acknowledgement obligation contains an unrelated preference
issues.rationale: The choice-selected clause says acknowledgement or Wi-Fi preference, and the route reason repeats this. T1 has no Wi-Fi preference. This is a source clarity discrepancy; the frozen T1 Boolean expectations themselves are consistent.
issues.required_revision: Remove the unrelated alternative in a separately sealed revision; do not silently edit this proposal.
